turns.t: Hello, doctor! I've brought my son Rohan with me because he keeps me right on dates. I'm Mr Kapoor. ~
Hi, doctor. Dad's been constipated since the iron tablets.
Pleased to meet you both. Mr Kapoor, when did the constipation start?
Oh, a month ago, six weeks, I really can't say, it crept up.
It's been two months, Dad, since they started the iron.
So between one and two months, we'll say. How often do you go to the toilet now?
Every three or four days. And it's hard. Pellets, like a rabbit.
Tell me about your medicines.
Ferrous sulphate, 200 mg, twice a day, for my anaemia. And metformin, 500 mg, twice a day, for my diabetes.
That fits. Iron is a very common cause of constipation. Do you have any family history of bowel problems?
His brother had bowel polyps, doctor. Removed, about ten years ago.
Thank you. And what do you eat, any fibre in your diet?
Rice, dal, a bit of chapatti. Not much fruit. I don't like it.
Let me feel your tummy.
Your tummy is soft, and I can feel some firm stool in the left lower side. Pulse is 72, blood pressure 130 over 82.
Is it serious? ~
Not usually, but because you're anaemic, and your brother had polyps, I'd like to look into why you needed the iron in the first place. ~
The iron was for tiredness. They found my blood low. ~
Yes, but not why it was low. I'd like to arrange a blood test, to see how the iron is responding, and I'll check on a bowel referral.
Can the iron be changed, so he's not blocked up? ~
Yes, we can try one tablet a day, or every other day, which is gentler. Take it with orange juice for absorption.
Every other day. All right. ~
And a stool softener, plus more fibre, prunes, brown bread, and plenty of water.
Prunes! My wife will be thrilled. ~
Will a lower dose of iron still work? ~
Yes, it replaces your stores more slowly, but it works, and you'll tolerate it better. ~
And how long until I'm not tired? ~
A few weeks, and the blood count will tell us how it's going. ~
I'd like to see you again in four weeks, with the blood results.
We'll be there. ~
